children: Barclays said concerns about CoreWeave’s bond troubles do not warrant alarm about the health of the broader AI sector. According to Sina Finance, the bank’s analysts said in a Monday report that investors need not fear a wider crisis even if the cloud infrastructure provider encounters further difficulties. Last week, yields on some CoreWeave bonds surged to 15%, and the company’s shares fell sharply. Barclays Global Head of Research Ajay Rajadhyaksha said investors should not extrapolate CoreWeave’s recent debt challenges to the broader AI capital expenditure cycle: the company’s unsecured bonds make up only a small part of its capital structure, its capital expenditure is a small share of total AI spending, and the major cloud providers responsible for most of that spending use different financing methods. He compared the concerns with the 2023 regional banking turmoil, saying investors had wrongly extrapolated regional banks’ problems to the entire U.S. economy. He also said the SPDR S&P Regional Banking ETF gave an extremely inaccurate signal about what would follow.

title: Barclays: Concerns Over CoreWeave Bond Selloff Are Overblown
